name: Hennesy, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Minnesota Constitution provides a reasonable expectation of privacy in cell phone location data, requiring a warrant, and while geofence warrants are not per se unconstitutional and probable cause existed, this specific warrant failed the particularity requirement due to unchecked police discretion in step two.

name: Hudson, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the court should have stayed the case pending the Supreme Court's decision in Chatrie but joined the majority opinion otherwise.

name: McKeig, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the court should have waited for the Supreme Court's guidance in Chatrie and that the majority failed to establish an adequate and independent state ground for its decision, relying too heavily on federal precedent.

name: Moore, III, J.
description: Dissented, argued that he joined in the dissent of Justice McKeig.

name: Gaïtas, J.
description: Other, argued that she took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Moore, III, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the punishment for unemployment benefit misrepresentation is not grossly disproportional to the offense and therefore does not violate the Excessive Fines Clauses.

name: Hennesy, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that courts must consider a person's ability to pay a fine when analyzing claims under the Excessive Fines Clause and that the case should be remanded to develop an evidentiary record on Thigpen's ability to pay.

name: Procaccini, Justice
description: Dissented, joined Justice Hennesy's dissent regarding the Minnesota Constitution's Excessive Fines Clause requiring consideration of an individual's ability to pay and that remand is appropriate.

name: HUDSON, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the 2024 amendment to attorney fee caps does not apply retroactively, the WCCA did not err in denying automatic approval of excess fees, the statutory fee cap does not violate the Contracts Clause, and the WCCA properly affirmed the denial of excess fees based on the Irwin factors.

name: PROCACCINI, J.
description: Recused from the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Procaccini, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Minnesota Statutes section 253D.20 establishes a waivable right to counsel for civilly committed persons, provided the waiver is knowing and intelligent.

name: Moore, III, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the right to counsel in civil commitment cases is non-waivable, citing concerns about practical effects, potential constitutional issues, and legislative intent.

name: Hennesy, J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Gaïtas, J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: FRANCIS J. CONNOLLY
description: Concurred, arguing that a suspended law license renders a person not "learned in the law" and thus constitutionally ineligible to serve as a supreme court justice, based on controlling precedent.

name: LESLIE E. BEIERS
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: JOHN H. GUTHMANN
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: TIMOTHY J. MCMANUS
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: LAURIE J. MILLER
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: HUDSON, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the recall petition failed to allege malfeasance because Jacobs' alleged conduct did not violate a substantive legal standard and she was not acting in her official capacity.

name: HENNESY, J.
description: Recused, not having been a member of the court at the time of submission, took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Anne K. McKeig
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: PROCACCINI, J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: CADISH, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Stadium Referendum was invalid because it violated the Nevada Constitution's full-text requirement and contained a legally inadequate and misleading description of effect.

name: STIGLICH, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: HERNDON, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: PARRAGUIRRE, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: BELL, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: PICKERING, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Stadium Referendum satisfied the Nevada Constitution's full-text requirement by reprinting the specific sections voters would disapprove and that its description of effect was adequate within the legal word limit.

name: LEE, J.
description: Concurred that the petition's description of effect was inadequate but dissented on the full-text requirement, agreeing with Justice Pickering that it was satisfied.

name: MOORE, III, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Emergency Management Act authorized the Governor to declare a peacetime emergency for the COVID-19 pandemic and does not unconstitutionally delegate legislative authority.

name: ANDERSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that while the Act does not violate separation of powers principles, the broad executive emergency powers raise serious concerns requiring legislative consideration for stronger checks.

name: Procaccini, J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: HUDSON, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that taxpayer standing is limited to cases involving alleged unlawful disbursements of public funds, and does not extend to challenging substantive laws based on incidental expenditures.

name: Hennesy, J.J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Gaïtas, J.J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: ANDERSON, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that an institution of purely public charity uses its property in furtherance of its charitable purpose when it leases property to its intended beneficiaries for personal residence.

name: ANDERSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the good-faith exception to the exclusionary rule does not extend to searches and arrests based on quashed warrants that appear active due to clerical errors by court administration, as applying the exclusionary rule in such cases deters unlawful government conduct and promotes judicial fairness.

name: PROCACCINI, J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Chutich, J.
description: Concurred, argued that racial imbalances alone are not sufficient to violate the Education Clause; a causal link to inadequate education must be proven.

name: Hudson, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that de facto segregation in public schools is sufficient, standing alone, to establish an Education Clause violation, and the causation requirement undermines the clause's purpose.

name: Procaccini, J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: THISSEN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the exclusion of the public from the courtroom was a 'true closure' implicating the public trial right, and the district court's findings were insufficient to determine if the closure was justified, requiring a remand for further findings on alternatives and scope.

name: McKEIG, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the district court's findings were sufficient to conclude that Bell's public trial right was not violated, especially considering the unprecedented circumstances of the COVID-19 pandemic and the court's adherence to public health guidance.

name: GILDEA, Chief Justice
description: Dissented, argued that she joined Justice McKeig's dissent.

name: ANDERSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that section 4.08 was integral to the proposed charter amendment's purpose, and severing it would deprive the amendment of its efficacy and strength, thus not reflecting the intent of the petition signers.

name: THISSEN, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the three valid sections of the proposed amendment should have been placed on the ballot as they stand on their own, and that the court should presume severability to protect the constitutional right of residents to govern themselves.

name: THISSEN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Article VII, Section 1, of the Minnesota Constitution requires an affirmative act of government to restore voting rights to felons, not automatic restoration upon release from incarceration, and that section 609.165 does not violate fundamental voting rights or equal protection.

name: ANDERSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the constitutional clause 'unless restored to civil rights' does not mean automatic restoration upon release from incarceration, and that section 609.165 does not violate Article VII, Section 1, but disagreed with the court's equal protection analysis method.

name: GILDEA, Chief Justice
description: Concurred with Justice Anderson's opinion.

name: HUDSON, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that section 609.165 is unconstitutional under heightened rational basis review because it creates a racial classification in practice, disproportionately affects communities of color, and undermines rehabilitation.

name: ANDERSON, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the tax court erred in denying summary judgment because the early childhood center provided undisputed evidence that it met the criteria for a tax-exempt seminary of learning.

name: ANDERSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the State presented sufficient evidence for conviction and the mandatory life sentence for a 21-year-old is not unconstitutionally cruel.

name: CHUTICH, Justice
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that while evidence was sufficient, a mandatory life sentence for a 21-year-old could be unconstitutionally cruel without an individualized sentencing hearing based on brain science.

name: THISSEN, Justice
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, agreed with Justice Chutich that an individualized sentencing hearing is needed to determine if a mandatory life sentence for a 21-year-old is unconstitutionally cruel.

name: ANDERSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the unanimity requirement for pardons is constitutional and does not violate the Minnesota Constitution's pardon or separation-of-powers provisions.

name: GILDEA, C.J.
description: Took no part in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: HUDSON, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that expanding a traffic stop to investigate a non-criminal pretrial release violation is an unlawful seizure under the Minnesota Constitution, as it requires reasonable articulable suspicion of criminal activity.

name: MOORE, III, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that while the decision is legally sound, it creates difficulties for law enforcement in enforcing pretrial release conditions related to public safety.

name: McKEIG, Justice
description: Concurred with Justice Moore's opinion.

name: THISSEN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the UMDDA provides a remedy only when untried complaints remain pending, and Mikell's constitutional speedy trial right was not violated.

name: ANDERSON, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the UMDDA's plain language unambiguously requires the State to bring untried charges to trial within 6 months and the majority's interpretation creates an unwritten exception.

name: GILDEA, C.J.
description: Dissented, joined in the dissent of Justice Anderson.

name: HUDSON, J.
description: Dissented, joined in the dissent of Justice Anderson.
